headline: Never Forget This Fibonacci-Shaped DP
problem_summary: You are climbing a staircase of n steps. Each time you can climb 1 or 2 steps. Return how many distinct ways you can climb to the top.
key_insight: The number of ways to reach step n is the sum of the ways to reach step n-1 and step n-2, since those are the only two steps you could have jumped from.
intuition: This is structurally identical to the Fibonacci recurrence: ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2), because every path to step n arrives via a final 1-step or a final 2-step move.

naive_approach.description: Plain recursion without memoization recomputes the same subproblems exponentially.

approach: Track only the last two values, a and b.
For each step from 3 to n, compute a + b and shift.
correctness: By induction: ways(1)=1 and ways(2)=2 are base cases; for n>2 every valid path's last move is either a 1-step from step n-1 or a 2-step from step n-2, and these two sets of paths are disjoint and exhaustive.

complexity.explanation: Single pass keeping only two running values.
